newsitem.title: USA: UAW to allow lower wages for new Ford parts units.
newsitem.headline: UAW to allow lower wages for new Ford parts units.

text.p: The United Auto Workers said Wednesday its tentative labor agreement allows Ford Motor Co to pay lower wages and benefits to workers in new parts businesses the automaker chooses to enter.

According to a summary of the proposed contract distributed to local leaders, Ford may pay workers in new parts businesses the prevailing wage and benefits for that industry segment or the geographic area in which it is located.
Ford and the UAW reached their tentative agreement Monday covering about 105,000 workers at the automaker.
The new parts provision, however, does not allow Ford to pay lower wages in new businesses that would compete with component work already covered by the UAW-Ford Master Agreement.
It also prohibits Ford from undercutting wages and benefits of non-Ford UAW workers in the same industry or geographic area.
UAW leaders expect the new pact to be ratified by September 29.
